title: fix: reduce session search stalls with large archives
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Broad `sessions_search` queries repeatedly materialize large archived session inventories on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

Searches keep the same visible active and archived sessions while doing less Gateway work. Requests are attributed as `sessions-search` in list diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery previously paged active and archived full rows across all agents, then repeated both scans for the requester's agent. It only consumes session identities and ownership relationships. One `dashboard` summary inventory preserves those facts. An exact requester-owned `global` lookup preserves the sentinel when another agent wins the combined listing, and is skipped when the inventory already supplied it. The embedded adapter now supports that metadata lookup too.

Search is on demand and rebuilds a fresh authorized inventory. A timestamp cursor alone would omit older searchable sessions; no retained authorization snapshot, new cache, configuration, or SQLite schema is introduced. Production grows by 35 lines including one generated validator line: the tool shrinks by 3, while the exact embedded lookup and bounded source tag account for the growth.

## Evidence

Synthetic workload: 3,500 sessions, 3,000 archived, four agents, real tool discovery through the embedded projection owner with serving Gateway state custody. Transcript FTS is excluded. Five counterbalanced A/B pairs per timing/allocation mode, three measured sweeps after two warmups, plus A/A controls. Baseline: `240d0ac7e9d3d`.

| Per discovery sweep | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| List requests | 30 | 18 |
| Returned list rows | 5,689 | 3,500 |
| Main-thread CPU, median run mean | 1,540.9 ms | 1,359.7 ms (-11.8%) |
| Sampled JS allocation, median run mean | 858.2 MiB | 619.6 MiB (-27.8%) |
| Elapsed, median run median | 1,868.7 ms | 1,729.1 ms |
| Elapsed p95, 15 measured sweeps | 2,168.5 ms | 2,158.6 ms |

The candidate includes one exact missing-global lookup in this fixture. Every run produces the same 3,501 search-key digest. CPU changes by pair: -13.6%, -7.8%, -31.5%, -26.1%, +6.0%; ranges are 1,408–1,574 ms before and 1,056–1,492 ms after. Timing A/A CPU was 2,082/2,303 ms as host load declined; allocation A/A differed by 0.07%. Cold first-discovery CPU medians are 2,098/2,023 ms. Cold elapsed run medians are 3,471/3,578 ms (+3.1%), while the median paired change is -2.1%; no cold latency improvement is claimed. Acceptance was unchanged candidate keys, fewer inventory operations, lower CPU/allocation, and no reproducible adverse latency.

CPU profiles also show lower row-materialization, model-fact, and roster-fact work. This is a session-metadata owner measurement, not a whole-Gateway or production deployment claim; transcript-database size and workspace-file populations are not simulated because this discovery workload does not search transcripts or walk workspaces.

Rerun from a fresh synthetic directory, then add `--reuse-fixture` for subsequent runs; alternate with/without `--source-ref` and use `--mode allocation` separately:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-prepared-list-measure.ts \
  --state-dir .local/search-discovery-bench --search-discovery --list-shape all \
  --sessions 3500 --archived-sessions 3000 --agents 4 --updates-per-list 0 \
  --iterations 3 --warmup 2 --plain-result --mode timing --source-ref 240d0ac7e9d3d
```

- The regression fails on the baseline after result assertions pass: 7,002 inventory rows exceed the 3,501 bound. The fix preserves active, archived, requester-global and foreign-global behavior.
- Isolated live Gateway plus a real model turn passed: the model invoked broad `sessions_search` through normal tool discovery/dispatch with no sessionKey filter. Persisted tool-result rows include the seeded active, archived, and requester-owned global sessions with their exact synthetic snippets. The Gateway used a private loopback port and isolated state; no existing Gateway was changed.
- Focused search tests 36/36; embedded adapter tests 29/29; protocol tests 20/20; affected UI browser 1/1 and UI E2E 4/4. Compiled protocol validators regenerated and checked; the UI production build succeeds.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed. Its own assertion annotation, fixture typing and shadowing failures were repaired, with the failed targeted checks green. The remaining dead-export failure reproduces identically on the exact parent: 56 production and 30 full-tree findings, with zero symbol differences. These are main regressions requiring repair, not noise.
- Final local Codex autoreview against `240d0ac7e9d3d`: scoped-clean at P0–P2. Author simplification removed the duplicate scan and redundant exact lookup. The 207-line test allocation covers the single-sweep regression, sentinel ownership/privacy, embedded exact lookup, and protocol-tag acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Exact-head inherited CI failures</summary>

[CI run 42955636343](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42955636343) completed on head `5da9c13c14903823a412b6eb43fe17a3ce5b6c31`. Its tested merge `223b71ef755b6c114784a26596bd085cf07cb4fa` combines actual main parent `e4696054e814730a6351f3b7bf5a35fc0fe2a793` with this head. Two jobs failed; the CI gate reports those downstream failures. All other selected jobs passed, including UI E2E, types, lint and Android.

- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-21`: two worker apply-patch containment assertions expect old recovery text. #194473 (`5d5c90e1e4e5a`) changed the policy-specific guidance without updating these assertions. Both cases fail identically on the exact CI main parent and this PR head (2 failed, 67 skipped).
- `checks-ui (3/3)`: the read-aloud test clicks its initial button before the intentionally deferred chat rows render. Commit `8e5ae5b37c5d1` removed the readiness wait. Exact CI main-parent production reproduces the same null-click failure when temporary test-only clock control forces the existing >15 ms admission path (1 failed, 14 skipped). This is controlled-timing evidence: the pristine original branch-parent full file passes 15/15. No production or assertion changes were used for the reproduction, and all diagnostic test instrumentation was removed.

Relevant tests and production owners are byte-identical between the actual CI main parent and tested merge. These are inherited main regressions requiring owner repair, not ignored failures. This PR includes no UI or worker-test changes and no CI rerun. The landing exception retains failed CI explicitly.

</details>
